description: OKLab and OKLCh, Ottosson (2020). The first four entries are the values Ottosson publishes in his introduction of the space, to three decimal places — the strongest kind of golden entry here, because they are numbers printed in the source rather than consequences of it. They are what catches a transcribed digit in M1 or M2, which is otherwise invisible: a wrong matrix still produces a smooth, plausible, perceptually-reasonable-looking space.

entries.derivationNote: Our D65 white [0.9504559270516716, 1, 1.0890577507598784] through M1, cube root, M2. NOT exactly [1, 0, 0]: the published matrices carry ten decimal places, and the residual is L = 0.999998801859709 with chroma 1.2515e-4. Ottosson's separate linear-sRGB-to-LMS matrix is tuned so white is exact, but using it would be a second path for one input space, against ADR-0003. Recorded and bounded rather than corrected — correcting it would mean using numbers no source publishes.
